out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: spicy beef soup on the stove was 107º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The PIC reheated the soup to 165º to correct.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: bean sprouts were 68º on the counter. Crispy shrimp rolls were 58º in the walk-in. Beef cooked yesterday was 48º in the prep unit. Cooked tofu was 58º in the walk-in. Wonton noodles were 63º in the walk-in. Raw shrimp was 55º in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All the foods listed above were discarded due to temperature abuse.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Clean and Sanitize
violations.observation: The manager was not able to explain how to properly set up and use the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall know that all utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be 1) washed with hot, soapy water to remove visible soil, 2) rinsed to remove residue, 3) sanitized using an approved sanitizer to reduce the number of bacteria and viruses and 4) air dried. Another manager arrived who was slightly more knowledgeable. The EHS trained both of them on how to properly wash rinse and sanitize equipment and how to check and adjust the warewashing machine when the sanitizer is too low. CDI.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed a large soup ladle stored in the kitchen handsink. Also observed the faucet spigot was turned towards the wall, making it difficult to wash hands.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. The ladle was moved during the inspection. The faucet spigot was moved too. There it’s only one here it must be available and it must be used for handwashing. Based on the today’s observations, the handsink was not being used and employees were not washing their hands in it. The EHS discussed the importance of handwashing with the manager. All employees washed their hands at least once during the visit, per the EHS request.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no hand soap available at the handsink in the cooking area.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The manager refilled the empty dispenser with hand soap, but the dispenser would not work. The manager then placed a bottle of handsoap at the handsink. CDI.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Cover Foods in Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped or uncovered food in the following location where the food is subject to contamination: several containers of food in the walk-in were not covered while in storage.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be protected from contamination by being stored in packages, covered containers or wrappings unless being cooled. Ensure all foods in the walk-in are covered, unless being cooled, during the follow-up.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the low temperature, chemical sanitizing warewashing machine was observed with a sanitizing rinse concentration of less than 50 ppm chlorine solution.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the three-compartment sink to manually wash, rinse and sanitize food-contact surfaces using a sanitizing solution at the proper concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine. The EHS primed the dishwashing unit which corrected the problem. The sanitizer rinse was 50 ppm. CDI.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The establishment uses bleach to sanitize and the three compartment sink and there was no bleach present at the start of the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. Bleach was acquired during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: several parts of the meat slicer were not clean with visible food debris present.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. Clean and sanitize the slicer prior to the follow-up.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: there were several foods out of temperature in the walk-in. A large container (~2 gallons) of beef soup cooked yesterday was 50º; a large container (~2 gallons) of chicken soup cooked yesterday was 49ºF; two packages of fresh bean sprouts were 49º and 48ºF; a container of peanut sauce was 48º; a box of egg rolls was 48º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All foods were discarded and the manager was advised to have the walk-in refrigerator serviced.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: egg rolls and other foods prepared on site were not being date marked.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The EHS explained the date marking requirements to the manager. Ensure all foods are date marked for the follow-up.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Observed glass cleaner and sanitizing wipes stored with food and equipment.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. The EHS explained how chemicals should be stored separately from food and equipment. The chemicals were moved during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Storage-Personal Care Items
violations.observation: Several personal care items such as acetaminophen, hand lotion, and bandages were being stored with food and equipment.
violations.corrective_action: All employees' personal care items shall be stored in a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces through improper labeling or storage. Store personal care items separate from food and food equipment to prevent contamination. Correct by the follow-up. PHO BOWL VIETNAMESE RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 12/31/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Air/Water Thermometers Accuracy, Only Degrees F
violations.observation: The ambient (air/water) temperature measuring device located in the walk-in refrigerator is reading 20ºF and not accurate.
violations.corrective_action: Ambient air and water temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to +/-3 degrees F in the intended range of use. Repair the unit thermometer or install an additional thermometer in the walk-in by the follow-up.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Ice As Coolant Not Used as Food
violations.observation: Ice used as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food is also for beverage ice or used as food. A one quart carton of half and half was being stored in the ice maker ice bin.
violations.corrective_action: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food, packaged foods, beverages, or cooling coils/tubes, the ice may not be used as food. The half and half was moved during the visit. CDI.

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: A bag of onions and two containers of shortening were being stored on the outside the back door on the pavement.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. The items were moved back inside during the inspection.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Cartons of canned soda were stored on the floor near the expo station.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Ensure no foods are stored on the floor during the follow-up.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: the handle for the ice scoop was stored in the ice maker ice during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The ice scoop was moved to its usual storage location on a clean plate on top of the ice maker during the inspection.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed several large pots stored outside the back of the establishment on the pavement.
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks. The pot were moved inside during the inspection.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: the ambient air temperature of the walk-in refrigerator was 46º and several TCS foods in it (beef broth, chicken broth, bean sprouts) were above 41º for more than 4 hours. A large plastic red colander in the three compartment sink was severely deteriorated (cracked, broken, melted, discolored) and is not longer cleanable.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Please have a qualified service technician service the unit as soon as possible. notify your EHS when corrected. Reinspection is required for this. The colander was discarded during the inspection.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not durable: observed chicken stock buckets being reused to store foods.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. Discontinue reusing manufacturer containers. Use NSF or equivalent food grade equipment to store foods. Several of the buckets were discarded during the inspection. Discard all other buckets prior to the follow-up.

violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. UNLESS FOOD IS COOLING, THE TEMPERATURE OF THE FOOD SHALL BE 41F OR BELOW AT ALL TIMES. FOOD SHALL BE DISCARDED AND A FOLLOW UP WILL OCCUR ON 6/23/2025.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: 1) NO DISCLOSURE STATEMENT THAT SAYS “THESE FOOD ITEMS MAY CONTAIN RAW AND/OR UNDERCOOKED INGREDIENTS” IS NOT PROVIDED ON THE MENU AND THE ASTERISK IS NOT LOCATED NEXT TO THE ACTUAL FOOD ITEM THAT IS ALLOWED TO BE ORDERED RAW AND/OR UNDERCOOKED (E.G. ROUND EYE).
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. ONCE RE-PRINTED, THE DISCLOSURE STATEMENT WILL BE PERMANENTLY PLACED ON THE MENU BEFORE THE REMINDER STATEMENT AND THE ASTERISK WILL BE PLACED DIRECTLY NEXT TO THE ROUND EYE. out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) LARGE PORTIONS OF COOKED FOODS SUCH AS SPRING ROLLS, NOODLES, GRILLED PORK, ETC ARE STORED IN DEEP, LARGE, COVERED CONTAINERS.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE MANAGER AGAIN PROPER COOLING METHODS TO INCLUDE TRANSFERRING THE FOOD INTO SHALLOW PANS, USING THE FREEZER, STIRRING AND MOVING THE FOOD AROUND EVERY 10-15 MINUTES TO RELEASE THE HEAT, USING ICE WANDS, AND CHECKING THE TEMPERATURE TO ENSURE IT COOLS FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS OR LESS AND FROM 135F TO 41F OR BELOW IN NO MORE THAN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS. IF THE FOOD DOES NOT REACH 70F IN 2 HOURS IT SHALL BE DISCARDED. ENSURE TRAINING TO STAFF BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP ON 6/23/2025.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name

violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO TRAIN STAFF TO CLEAN THE WORKING CONTAINERS DAILY AND RE-LABEL THEM DAILY. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP ON 6/23/2025.

violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT THAT HAND SINKS ARE FOR HAND WASHING PURPOSES ONLY. ENSURE RE-TRAINING TO STAFF BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at the kitchen handwashing sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO PROVIDE SOAP. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at the bar and kitchen handwashing sinks used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP THAT ALL HAND SINKS SHALL BE SUPPLIED WITH THE SIGNAGE REMINDING STAFF TO WASH HANDS. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: 1) RAW SHELLED EGGS STORED ON A SHELF ABOVE VEGETABLES INSIDE THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO ORGANIZE THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR SO ALL RAW ANIMAL PROTEINS LIKE RAW EGGS, RAW PORK, RAW SEAFOOD, RAW BEEF, AND RAW POULTRY ARE STORED ON ONLY THE LOWEST SHELVES TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION. STAFF WERE TO REORGANIZE THE UNIT TODAY AFTER DISCARDING FOOD DUE TO IMPROPER COLD TEMPERATURES. ENSURE PROPER STORAGE OF RAW ANIMAL FOODS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) ALL FOOD STORED INSIDE THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO INCLUDE BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE FOLLOWING: A) UNSALTED BUTTER: 52F, B) SPRING ROLLS: 52F, C) COOKED CHICKEN: 52F, D) COOKED BRISKET: 52F, E) BEAN SPROUTS: 54F, F) FRIED TOFU: 52F, G) RAW CHICKEN: 54F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO DISCARD ALL FOODS AS THEY ARE NOT HOLDING AT 41F OR BELOW AND OWNERSHIP DID NOT KNOW WHEN THE UNIT STOPPED WORKING. EHS REMINDED OWNERSHIP THAT FOOD TEMPERATURES SHALL BE CHECKED EACH MORNING UPON ARRIVAL TO ENSURE REFRIGERATION UNITS ARE WORKING AND FOOD IS COLD AS REQUIRED. FOODS WERE DISCARDED UPON REQUEST. PHO BOWL VIETNAMESE RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 12/10/2024) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: 1) BEAN SPROUTS, 2) COOKED NOODLES, 3) SOMETIMES BOBA.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP. THE ABOVE LISTED FOODS WILL BE ON TIME. EHS REMINDED OWNERSHIP THAT THE FOODS SHALL HAVE A START TEMPERATURE OF EITHER 41F OR BELOW OR 135F OR ABOVE. ONCE THOSE TEMPERATURES ARE TAKEN THAT STARTS THE 4 HOUR TIME ALLOWANCE. DOCUMENTATION IS REQUIRED AT ALL TIMES. SEE THE AGREEMENT PROVIDED IN EMAIL. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: 1) NO DISCLOSURE STATEMENT IS PROVIDED ON THE MENU AND THE ASTERISK IS NOT PROVIDED NEXT TO THE FOOD ITEM THAT IS ALLOWED TO BE UNDERCOOKED (E.G. ROUND EYE).
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. EHS DISCUSSED THE PROPER DISCLOSURE STATEMENT AND WHERE THE ASTERISK SHALL BE PLACED WHEN NEW MENUS ARE TO BE PRINTED IN JANUARY. PLEASE PROVIDE A ROUGH COPY OF THE NEW MENU DURING THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed chemicals, first aid items, and/or personal care items stored on a shelf above work surfaces in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP THAT ALL CHEMICALS SHALL BE STORED BELOW AND SEPARATE FROM FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, CLEAN LINENS, AND SINGLE SERVICE ITEMS USED FOR CUSTOMERS. EHS ALSO DISCUSSED THAT STAFF’S PERSONAL CARE ITEMS SHALL BE SEPARATE. DESIGNATE ONE AREA FOR STAFF’S STORAGE OF PERSONAL ITEMS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) LARGE BATCHES OF COOKED NOODLES ARE STORED IN SEALED TAKE HOME BAGS INSIDE THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO TRAIN STAFF ON HOW TO COOL DOWN HOT FOODS RAPIDLY. THIS INCLUDES USING SHALLOW PORTIONS ON SHEET TRAYS AND USING FREEZERS, ICE BATHS, ICE WANDS, SMALL PORTIONS, NO COVERS, ETC. ENSURE STAFF ARE TRAINED ON COOLING BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP. SEE FACT SHEET PROVIDED IN ENGLISH AND SPANISH ON COOLING ATTACHED TO THE EMAIL.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: 1) SQUEEZE BOTTLES OF CONDIMENTS, SAUCES, WATER, VINEGAR, OIL, ETC, 2) BULK BINS FOR SUGAR, SALT, ETC.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO LABEL ALL WORKING CONTAINERS OF FOODS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed food directly stored on the floor in the kitchen and walk-in refrigerator. This included canned goods, oil, etc.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO GET THE FOOD ITEMS OFF THE FLOOR USING PROPER SHELVING UNITS OR DUNNAGE RACKS; NO CRATES OF ANY KIND (E.G. SODA, MILK, PRODUCE, OR DISH RACKS). ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wipings Clothes Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO STORE WET TOWELS IN CONTAINERS WITH A BLEACH WATER SOLUTION MAINTAINED AT 50-200PPM. ONLY CLEAN, DRY TOWELS MAY SIT ON WORK SURFACES BETWEEN USES. DIRTY TOWELS ARE ALWAYS IN A DIRTY LINEN BAG OR CONTAINER FOR LAUNDERING. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) IN-USE UTENSILS IN WATER, 2) ICE SCOOP LYING IN THE ICE MACHINE AT THE BAR, 3) PLASTIC QUART CUP TO DISPENSE RICE.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP PROPER IN-USE UTENSIL STORAGE. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION AND TRAINING TO STAFF BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Clean equipment and utensils such as pots, pans, forks, spoons, etc were observed stored with the food-contact surface facing upward.
violations.corrective_action: Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered/inverted. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP THAT ALL CLEANED AND SANITIZED EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS SHALL BE STORED UPSIDE DOWN ON SHELVING. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers for chicken base powder were observed reused for the storage of other foods.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP THAT CHICKEN BASE BUCKETS, TOFU BUCKETS, PEELED GARLIC CONTAINERS, SPICE CONTAINERS, SRIRACHA BOTTLES, ETC ARE NOT TO BE REUSED AS THEY DO NOT WITHSTAND THE CONSTANT WARE WASHING PROCESS. REPLACE REUSED ITEMS WITH NSF APPROVED FOOD CONTAINERS DESIGNED FOR CONTINUOUS REUSE BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not durable: 1) OBSERVED STAFF USING THE TAKE OUT BAGS FOR FOOD STORAGE IN BOTH REFRIGERATORS AND FREEZERS.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP STORING ALL FOOD IN NSF APPROVED FOOD CONTAINERS OR FOOD GRADE PLASTIC BAGS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: Observed the following in poor repair: 1) WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR OBSERVED OPERATING AT 51F, 2) BURNT OUT LIGHT BULBS IN THE KITCHEN CEILING AND UNDER THE HOOD.
violations.corrective_action: EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO CALL FOR IMMEDIATE SERVICE ON THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR AS IT SHALL OPERATE BETWEEN 34F-38F TO KEEP FOODS AT 41F OR BELOW. EHS ALSO INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO REPLACE ANY BURNT OUT LIGHT BULBS. ENSURE CORRECTION OF BOTH ITEMS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Garbage and refuse properly disposed, facilities maintained

violations.title: Receptacles, Provided for Paper Towel Disposal
violations.observation: There is no refuse container at the area immediately adjacent to the kitchen area hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: If disposable paper towels are used at handwashing sinks, a trash can shall be located at each sink or group of adjacent sinks. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP THAT SMALL TRASH CANS FOR DISPOSAL OF PAPER TOWELS NEED TO BE UNDER OR CLOSE TO HAND SINKS. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed that the kitchen walls and ceiling panels are in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP THAT THE PHYSICAL FACILITIES INCLUDE FLOORS, WALLS, BASE BOARDS, AND CEILING PANELS. THESE SHALL BE CLEANED REGULARLY TO REMOVE GREASE, FOOD DEBRIS, FOOD SPLATTER, MOLD, DUST, ETC. EHS ALSO DISCUSSED MAKING SURE ALL CEILING PANELS ARE INTACT AND SEALED TO PREVENT POSSIBLE INSECT ENTRY OVER TIME. ENSURE CLEANING IS COMPLETED BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP AND OWNERSHIP CONSIDERS REPLACEMENT OF ALL KITCHEN CEILING PANELS WITH NEW VINYL COATED PANELS IF NOT CLEANABLE.
